https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120372.title: US-Sanktionen gegen Havanna | USA kehrt in Kuba zurück zum Kolonialismus des weißen Mannes
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120372.author: Christian Klemm
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120372.text:
- Kommentare
- US-Sanktionen gegen Havanna
USA kehrt in Kuba zurück zum Kolonialismus des weißen Mannes
Washington erlässt neue Sanktionen gegen den Inselstaat. Der Verlust von Menschenleben ist dabei einkalkuliert. Ein Kommentar.
Die Bösartigkeit dieser US-Administration ist kaum noch zu toppen. Nachdem die Regierung von Donald Trump mit einer Seeblockade Kuba von internationalen Öllieferungen fast vollständig abgeschnitten hat, holt Washington zum nächsten Schlag aus – diesmal gegen die kubanische Elektroindustrie: Am Donnerstag (Ortszeit) gab das dortige Außenministerium bekannt, erstmals zwei chinesische Elektronikunternehmen auf die Sanktionsliste zu setzen. Sie werden beschuldigt, der kubanischen Armee Elektronik und Sicherheitskomponenten zu verkaufen. Die Begründung ist ein Meisterstück antikubanischer Rabulistik aus dem Weißen Haus: Die »herrschende Elite« in dem Karibikstaat eigne sich Energieressourcen und maritime Transportmittel an und lasse »das kubanische Volk mit Stromausfällen, Treibstoffknappheit und einer darbenden Wirtschaft zurück«.
Für die aktuellen Stromausfälle, Treibstoffknappheit und die großen Wirtschaftsprobleme Kubas ist jedoch nicht die »herrschende Elite« dort verantwortlich, sondern einzig und alleine die »blonden Bestien« (Augusto César Sandino) aus dem Norden. Die verfolgen nämlich ein großes Ziel: die Karibikinsel wieder zu dem machen, was es zur Zeit der Batista-Diktatur war, die von der Revolution 1959 hinweggefegt wurde: ein Spielerparadies und Bordell vor allem für US-amerikanische Touristen mit haufenweise Dollars im Gepäck.
Unser Kollege Johannes Hecht befindet sich zurzeit auf Kuba. Seine Eindrücke von der Karibikinsel könnt ihr hier in einem Kurzvideo sehen.
Die neuen Sanktionen sind vor allem ein Problem für die kubanische Solarindustrie, weil Havanna beim Aufbau seiner Solarparks auf chinesische Technologie angewiesen ist. Die Volksrepublik in Fernost hat sich seit Jahren zu einem zuverlässigen Handelspartner für die Genossen in der Karibik erwiesen. Wenn sie nun durch die USA sanktioniert werden, ist das für Peking wirtschaftlich leicht zu verkraften. Für Kuba allerdings ist das eine Verschärfung seiner chronischen Energieknappheit. Durch sie ist beispielsweise schon jetzt die Gesundheitsversorgung der Bevölkerung betroffen. Auch die Nahrungsmittelproduktion ist auf Strom angewiesen. Das heißt in der Konsequenz: Die Trump-Regierung kalkuliert für ihr politisches Ziel, die Insel von »den Castros zu befreien« (Nota bene: Einer lebt schon nicht mehr.), den Verlust von Menschenleben mit ein.
Der ehemalige US-Präsident Barack Obama hatte eine vorsichtige Annäherung zwischen den USA und Kuba begonnen. Donald Trump hat diese nicht nur abgebrochen, sondern die Entwicklung durch seine beinharte Hinterhofpolitik in Lateinamerika umgekehrt: Der weiße Mann aus dem industrialisierten Norden gibt wieder den Ton an. So wie zu Zeiten des Kolonialismus.
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.
Keine Paywall, kein Kleingedrucktes, nur ein Ziel: dass nd bleibt.

https://gothamist.com/arts-entertainment.title: When turning back the clock means going under an NYC sidewalk
https://gothamist.com/arts-entertainment.author: Hannah Frishberg
https://gothamist.com/arts-entertainment.text:
Time waits for no man — except Gilo Vintimilla, the master jeweler whose expertise is required to turn back the hands on the only clock embedded in a New York City sidewalk.
“There?” he asks his phone in a lilting Ecuadorian accent as he balances on top of a ladder beneath the sidewalk, carefully adjusting the clock’s minute hand from below.
“No, no, too far, come back,” responds Brianna Thompson, as she observes the clockface from street level. Thompson is marketing director for William Barthman Jeweler — the very company that installed the clock here on the corner of Maiden Lane in 1899 as a novelty advertisement in front of the business's original location. “Wait, no, too far, come forward.”
Of the many New York City clocks that don’t automatically update for daylight saving time, few require as much manual care as the Financial District’s pavement timepiece. But despite the hassle, Vintimilla has been loyally descending into this basement since 2001 every time the clock needs a fix.
“It's a labor of love. The clock is his baby,” Thompson explains after we ascend to the street and Vintimilla flits away to William Barthman’s current location a few blocks away. Meanwhile, the Wall Street lunch crowd appears none the wiser about time’s mechanical passage, as people rush past and periodically over (and on) the clock.
It’s a tough baby to love: Some 50,000 people a day walk over its sapphire crystal cover. In addition to adjusting for daylight saving, Vintimilla must periodically jiggle the face to get off dirt, lest it get in the mechanisms. Around 2014, a hand truck rolled over the clock and broke the glass. In 2001, the force of the Twin Towers’ collapse sent a crack through the sidewalk, the clock and the adjacent building. Vintimilla fitted the clock with a fresh new face and cover; the crack is still visible in the sidewalk and building.
Recently, the residential conversion of that building, 174 Broadway, turned the basement in which the clock is powered into a wreckage-filled pit of broken beams and rubble. Vintimilla plans to readjust the clock face soon to make sure it’s level, an endeavor that will likely require temporarily removing it from its subterranean perch.
When he’s not fixing the clock, he’s fixing just about everything else, from eyeglasses and jewelry to handbags and shoes, or doing custom jewelry design. Though he’s trained by various vendors, including Rolex, he’s mostly self-taught.
Since the William Barthman company installed the timepiece here over 120 years ago, maintaining it has always been a challenge met by impassioned jewelers. When its original designer died in 1917, no one could maintain the mechanical oddity, and so it was replaced with a version that could be. Today, the clock may be fixed in history and concrete, but its upkeep is dependent on Vintimilla and whoever pays 174 Broadway’s Con Ed bill.
Its preservation, however, is spiritually important, says clock enthusiast and recently licensed NYC Tour Guide Suzanne Dirks, handing me a sheet of custom clock stickers as we stand under scaffolding, gazing at the clock’s stalwart — if grime-spotted — compass.
“The clock is a window in time. A relic of time. It's seen so much change,” she waxes as tourists stumble by, intermittently looking up and at their phones.
In our digital world, such analog heirlooms are no longer necessary to determine the hour, but, Dirks says, "I think we still desperately need them because they’re reminders that there’s an IRL world where we are connected by these anchors, that time is shared amongst New Yorkers.”

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Papa Leão XIV envia mensagem a Lula; presidente responde com convite para visitar o Brasil
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Giuliana Tiberi
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) recebeu, nesta sexta-feira (6), uma mensagem do papa Leão XIV com votos de paz e unidade para o Brasil. O contato ocorreu enquanto o pontífice sobrevoava o território brasileiro a caminho do Uruguai, primeira parada de sua viagem pela América do Sul.
Lula agradeceu o gesto e relacionou as palavras do líder da Igreja Católica ao compromisso de construir um país mais justo, destacando a importância da união entre os brasileiros.
“Que as bênçãos de Deus nos ajudem a governar para todos os brasileiros e que nossa nação siga unida rumo a um futuro de paz, esperança e justiça para todos”, escreveu o petista nas redes sociais.
O presidente também aproveitou a ocasião para renovar o convite ao pontífice. “O povo brasileiro receberá Sua Santidade com muito carinho, acolhimento e fé”, afirmou.
Viagem pela América Latina
Leão XIV desembarcou nesta sexta-feira em Montevidéu, capital do Uruguai, dando início a uma agenda que também inclui Argentina e Peru.
Antes de chegar ao destino, enviou saudações a Lula, invocando sobre o Brasil “os dons da unidade e da paz de Deus Todo-Poderoso”.
A troca de mensagens segue uma tradição diplomática do Vaticano, que costuma cumprimentar os chefes de Estado dos países sobrevoados durante viagens internacionais.
A visita à América Latina também representa um retorno a uma região importante da trajetória de Leão XIV, que atuou como missionário e bispo no Peru antes de assumir a liderança da Igreja Católica.
O Brasil não está entre os destinos previstos nesta viagem, e ainda não há confirmação de uma futura passagem do papa pelo país.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.title: Dončić dazzles with 53 in Lakers’ win as LeBron held to eight in Cleveland return
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.author: Agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.text:
Luka Dončić scored 53 points and hit a key jumper in the lane with 28 seconds to play, carrying Los Angeles to a victory over Portland.
Dončić produced his 11th career 50-point game and his fourth with Los Angeles while preserving a fourth straight win for the Lakers, whose late 12-point lead had dwindled to four before Dončić and Austin Reaves combined to score 10 points in the final seconds.
Reaves scored 25 points and Walker Kessler had 16 points and 12 rebounds for the Lakers, who avenged a 136-129 home loss to Portland on October 27 with this NBA Cup victory.
Dončić scored 20 points in the third quarter alone to hit 40 for the sixth time in an incredible seven-game surge that includes six 40-point games – including four straight – and a 37-point performance.
The Slovenian superstar added five assists and five rebounds, giving him seven consecutive games with at least 35 points, five assists, five rebounds and five three-pointers.
Deni Avdija had 22 points, 11 assists and nine rebounds and Damian Lillard scored 22 points for the Blazers, who lost for only the second time this season in the finale of their four-game road trip.
Philadelphia 76ers 95-119 Cleveland Cavaliers
Donovan Mitchell scored 23 points as the Cleveland Cavaliers held LeBron James to eight points in his return to Northeast Ohio and rolled to a 119-95 victory over the Philadelphia 76ers in an NBA Cup group-stage game Friday night.
James – who elected to sign with Philadelphia in the offseason instead of returning for a third stint with Cleveland – was three of 12 from the field, including zero for four on three-pointers, in 31 minutes. James received a smattering of boos from Cavaliers fans every time he touched the ball during the first half and left the game with 3:54 remaining.
It was only the 10th time in his 24-year career that James has scored in single digits in the regular season. The Akron, Ohio, native’s NBA-record run of 1,297 consecutive regular-season games with at least 10 points ended on December 4 last season in the Los Angeles Lakers’ victory at Toronto.
Evan Mobley added 22 points for the Cavaliers, who bounced back after two losses to Oklahoma City. Mitchell also had seven rebounds and eight assists in 33 minutes. James Harden scored 17.
It was a rough night for the 76ers, who lost for only the second time in 10 games this season. They shot 36.5% from the field, including 10 of 40 on three-pointers.
Jaylen Brown led Philadelphia with 20 points, VJ Edgecombe scored 19 and Tyrese Maxey had 17. Joel Embiid missed all nine of his shots from the field but was six of six from the line.
Boston Celtics 119-80 Charlotte Hornets
Jayson Tatum had 34 points, nine assists and eight rebounds, Derrick White added 18 points and Boston demolished Charlotte for their seventh win in eight games.
Boston shot 17 of 31 from three-point range in the first half to build a 31-point lead and improved to 2-0 in NBA Cup play. The Hornets fell to 0-2.
Naz Reid had 14 points for Charlotte, who have lost six straight since coach Charles Lee benched Reid – the team’s biggest offseason acquisition – in the second half of a game against the Detroit Pistons because he did not meet “team standards”.
This one was over early.
Tatum erupted for 18 points in the first quarter on three three-pointers and White added 10 as the Celtics bolted to a 40-20 lead. Boston made nine of 17 three-pointers in the first quarter.
Charlotte couldn’t do anything right.
The Hornets shot 28% from the field in the opening half while turning the ball over eight times.
Tatum remained in the game until the final minute of the third quarter with Boston up 42 as the Celtics padded their point differential numbers for the NBA Cup.
Washington Wizards 132-139 Atlanta Hawks
Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 28 points and Atlanta held off Washington in an NBA Cup game.
It was the third straight win for the Hawks and second straight against the Wizards, as Atlanta swept the home-and-home series.
Trae Young had 23 points, 10 assists and a season-high eight turnovers in his first game in Atlanta as a visitor after being traded last season after seven-plus years with the Hawks.
Lu Dort had 25 points, including a crucial shot-clock-beating corner jumper late in the fourth quarter. Onyeka Okongwu scored 22 points and Aaron Wiggins added 19 points off the bench for Atlanta. Dyson Daniels guarded Young for much of the game and finished with 13 points and 12 assists.
Kyshawn George scored 33 points for the Wizards, who were without Anthony Davis (sprained right ankle). Tre Johnson had 23 points, including five three-pointers.
The Hawks pushed the pace the entire game, and their 139 points were a season high. It was also the most points the Wizards have surrendered this season. The Hawks shot 53% (52 for 98) from the field and 42% (16 for 38) from three-point range.
Toronto Raptors 121-107 Milwaukee Bucks
Alijah Martin scored a career-high 27 points and RJ Barrett also had 27 as short-handed Toronto defeated Milwaukee in an NBA Cup game.
Toronto outscored Milwaukee 70-47 in the second half to improve to 1-1 while the Bucks fell to 0-1 in NBA Cup group play. They’re part of East Group A along with Detroit, Orlando and Brooklyn.
The Raptors were playing without seven-time All-NBA selection Kawhi Leonard (knee), two-time All-Star Scottie Barnes (groin) or starting guard Immanuel Quickley (hamstring). Leonard missed his seventh straight game.
Martin picked up the slack by shooting nine of 11 overall and six of seven from three-point range. He entered Friday having gone six of 27 on three-point attempts in his career.
The 2025 second-round pick from Florida hadn’t scored more than nine points in any of his previous 30 career games. Martin had totaled 23 points in seven games this season before his breakthrough Friday.
Toronto’s Jamal Shead added a career-high 16 assists along with 10 points. Collin Murray-Boyles and Jakob Poeltl had 19 points each.
Milwaukee’s Tyler Herro had 23 points and 10 assists. Bucks rookie Brayden Burries had 21 points and 11 rebounds to set career highs in both categories.
Oklahoma City Thunder 128-97 Memphis Grizzlies
Ajay Mitchell scored a career-high 35 points, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander added 28 and Oklahoma City beat Memphis in an NBA Cup group-stage game.
Oklahoma City have won 16 straight over Memphis, including a four-game sweep in the first round of the 2025 playoffs.
Jared McCain finished with 21 points for the Thunder, who shot 55%.
Ty Jerome led Memphis with 21 points and Zach Edey added 14. Rookie Cameron Boozer was limited to eight points but grabbed 12 rebounds.
Oklahoma City benefited from a strong shooting night. In the closing minutes of the third quarter, the Thunder were converting at just under a 60% clip. They made half of their 26 three-point attempts through three periods.
Oklahoma City also forced 18 turnovers, turning them into 30 points.
Utah Jazz 100-112 Dallas Mavericks
Cooper Flagg scored 21 points and Kyrie Irving added 14 after a sluggish first half for both stars as Dallas beat Utah in an NBA Cup game Friday night.
PJ Washington scored 22 of his season-high 26 points in a first half that ended in a 57-all tie, setting the stage for Flagg and Irving to take over after the break.
Flagg scored 17 in the second half, while Irving had all but two of his points after halftime after starting one of 11 from the field. While Flagg’s scoring lagged before the break, he had six rebounds and assists in the first half before finishing with 10 and seven, respectively.
Lauri Markkanen scored 24 points and rookie Darryn Peterson had 21 for the Jazz, who lost their seventh straight game to drop to 1-8.
Flagg and Irving scored 21 of the points on a 22-10 run that turned a one-point Dallas deficit into an 81-70 lead late in the third quarter. Flagg had 13 points and Irving eight.
Minnesota Timberwolves 115-109 New Orleans Pelicans
Ayo Dosunmu scored 26 points in Minnesota’s victory over New Orleans.
With the victory, the Timberwolves (7-3) remained unbeaten in NBA Cup play, moving to 2-0. New Orleans (4-5), whose four-game winning streak was snapped in the loss, dropped to 0-1 in Cup play.
Dejounte Murray’s three-pointer gave New Orleans an 89-87 lead with 7:55 to go in the game, but LaMelo Ball responded with five consecutive points, igniting a 10-2 run by the Timberwolves to give them a 97-91 advantage. Minnesota would hold on to the lead for the remainder of the game.
Ball finished the game with 22 points and eight assists. Jaden McDaniels added 23 points in the win for the Timberwolves.
Jeremiah Fears led the way for the Pelicans with 24 points and Saddiq Bey had 17. Zion Williamson, who entered the night averaging 21.5 points per game, scored a season-low 13 points for New Orleans.
San Antonio Spurs 124-109 Sacramento Kings
Victor Wembanyama had 30 points and 14 rebounds and San Antonio beat Sacramento in an NBA Cup game.
Wembanyama, coming off a 52-point, 24-rebound game in a victory over Dallas on Wednesday, recorded his seventh double-double of the season, tied for third place in the NBA with Sacramento’s Domantas Sabonis, who finished with 17 points and 12 rebounds.
Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell and Dylan Harper scored 19 points apiece and Harrison Barnes added 13 for the Spurs (7-2).
The Spurs scored 75 points in the first half and led by 19 at the break. They extended their lead to as many as 24 points midway through the fourth quarter. San Antonio’s 75-point first half was their second-highest scoring half of the season behind their 80-point half against the Kings on October 27.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120372.title: Metall- und Elektroindustrie in Berlin | Stillstand am Fließband
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120372.author: Christian Lelek
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120372.text:
- Berlin
- Metall- und Elektroindustrie in Berlin
Stillstand am Fließband
Noch keine Lösung im Tarifkonflikt der Metall- und Elektroindustrie. In Berlin und Brandenburg ist die IG Metall offen für phasenweisen Lohnverzicht.
Es scheinen vor allem die Arbeitgeber zu sein, die in den Angriffsmodus geschaltet haben. »Die IG Metall schürt bei ihren Leuten Erwartungen von einem anderen Stern«, schäumte Henning Brandes, Verhandlungsführer des Verbands der Metall- und Elektroindustrie in Berlin und Brandenburg (VME). Und weiter: »Mit Plakaten und Trillerpfeifen wird es nicht gelingen, die Probleme unserer Branche aus der Welt zu schaffen. Das gelingt nur am Verhandlungstisch.«
An diesem waren zuvor am Freitag die Verhandlungen zwischen dem VME und der IG Metall ergebnislos zu Ende gegangen. Die ganze Woche über hatte die IG Metall zahlreiche Betriebe bestreikt, auch noch am Freitag. Bis zur Wochenmitte zählte die Gewerkschaft 7000 Mitglieder, die ihre Arbeit mindestens zeitweise niedergelegt hatten.
Die Arbeitgeber verbreiteten ihrerseits düstere Zukunftsperspektiven. Den Abbau von branchenweit 300.000 Jobs stellte Gesamtmetall für die kommenden zwei bis drei Jahre in Aussicht und damit mit 3,4 Millionen Beschäftigten den niedrigsten Stand in dieser Branche seit der Wiedervereinigung. Seit 2019 seien bereits 350.000 Arbeitsplätze abgebaut worden. Wie zur Bestätigung hatte nur einen Tag vorher der Autozulieferer Schaeffler den Abbau von Arbeitsplätzen hauptsächlich in Deutschland verkündet. Der Standort in Berlin, wo unter anderem Elektromotoren und Antriebstechnologien entwickelt werden, soll komplett schließen. Dadurch fallen 259 Stellen weg.
Die Arbeitgeber führen ihre Zurückhaltung in der laufenden Tarifrunde auf die fortwährende Krise zurück: fehlende Aufträge, steigende Kosten und immer schärfere Konkurrenz aus dem Ausland. »Die extrem schwierige Lage bei dem Großteil unserer Betriebe verbietet es, Arbeit noch weiter zu verteuern«, sagte VME-Verhandlungsführer Brandes. »Die Strukturprobleme lassen sich nicht wegstreiken.«
Die IG Metall hält das bisherige Vorgehen der Arbeitgeber für das falsche Krisenmanagement. »Verzicht ist keine Zukunftsstrategie und sichert keinen Arbeitsplatz und keinen Standort. Das geht nur mit Investitionen und Innovationen in die Werke bei uns in der Region«, sagte Jan Otto, Leiter des Bezirks Berlin-Brandenburg-Sachsen.
Nichtsdestotrotz legte die IG Metall am Freitag ein Konzept vor, mit dem »Investitionen in Zukunftsprodukte mit verbindlichen Zusagen für Standorte, Arbeitsplätze und Ausbildung verbunden werden«. Eine Tarifforderung der IG Metall ist die Absicherung von Standorten und Arbeitsplätzen. Das nun vorgelegte Konzept soll als Tarifvertrag für klar begrenzte Fälle vereinbart werden. Wie ein Sprecher auf Nachfrage von »nd« mitteilte, müssten Details hierzu noch ausverhandelt werden. Aus Sicht der IG Metall könne das aber auch den phasenweisen Verzicht auf Teile des Lohns bedeuten.
Während die IG Metall am einen Ende auf schwache Unternehmen Rücksicht nehmen will, fordert sie von profitablen Unternehmen für ihre Mitglieder eine Gewinnbeteiligung. Das Bild der Arbeitgeber von einer »Krise überall« entspreche nicht der Realität, sagte der IG Metall-Sprecher weiter.
Die Gewerkschaft verweist auch mit Blick auf ihre Lohnforderungen auf sich bessernde Konjunkturprognosen. Das bisherige Angebot der Arbeitgeber, die Gehälter erst im Juli 2028 um 1,3 Prozent anzuheben, bezeichnete Bezirksleiter Otto als ein »freches Minus-Angebot«, das hinter die allgemeinen Preissteigerungen zurückfalle. Die IG Metall war mit einer Forderung von fünf Prozent mehr Gehalt bei einer Vertragslaufzeit von zwölf Monaten in die Tarifrunde gegangen.
Die Arbeitgeber bezeichneten ihren Vorschlag als ein Zeichen des Entgegenkommens. Sie wiesen darauf hin, dass es erst im April dieses Jahres 3,1 Prozent mehr Geld für die 96.000 Beschäftigten in Berlin und Brandenburg gegeben habe.
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.
Keine Paywall, kein Kleingedrucktes, nur ein Ziel: dass nd bleibt.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120373.title: Gesundheitsinformation | Eisen im Spinat, Wunderkuren und Impfmythen
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120373.author: Ulrike Henning
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120373.text:
- Wirtschaft und Umwelt
- Gesundheitsinformation
Eisen im Spinat, Wunderkuren und Impfmythen
Ärzte in Deutschland müssen sich zunehmend mit medizinischen Fake-News auseinandersetzen – nicht zuletzt zum Schutz ihrer Patienten
Der fälschlicherweise zu hoch angesetzte Eisengehalt von Spinat könnte als eine frühe Fehlinformation in Medizin oder Ernährungswissenschaft gelten. Die Geschichte ist verwickelter als angenommen, denn es ging nicht einfach um einen Kommafehler, der jahrzehntelang abgeschrieben wurde. Vielmehr hatte Ende des 19. Jahrhunderts ein Physiologe den Wert korrekt für getrocknetes Spinatpulver ermittelt. Dieser wurde dann falsch frischem Spinat zugeordnet, und das wurde immer wieder übernommen. Die Fehlinformation wirkte nachhaltig und führte bei Aufdeckung zu dem ebenfalls falschen Schluss, dass Spinat überhaupt nicht so gesund sei. Ist er wohl doch – immer noch als ergiebige Eisenquelle mit drei bis vier Milligramm pro 100 Gramm.
Immerhin scheint das nun nach Jahrzehnten den meisten klar zu sein. Mittlerweile jedoch hat die Medizin nicht nur mit Fehlinformationen zu tun. »Es geht eindeutig um Desinformation, also um beabsichtigte Fehlinformation«, erklärt Susanne Johna. Die Vorsitzende des Marburger Bundes (MB) ist Internistin, Krankenhaushygienikerin und Gesundheitsökonomin. Bei der derzeit in Berlin stattfindenden Hauptversammlung der Ärztegewerkschaft MB ist die Auseinandersetzung mit den Medizin-Fakes ebenfalls als Thema gesetzt.
Wie auch im Spinatfall geht eine Richtigstellung »nicht in einer Minute«, muss Johna zugestehen. Und sie braucht Überzeugungsbereitschaft. In einer auf Effizienz getrimmten Medizin bleibe dafür kaum Zeit. Zwei Aspekte sind der Ärztin und Berufspolitikerin wichtig: Zum einen schaden die Patienten sich selbst, wenn sie den Fakes auf den Leim gehen. Ihre Ängste werden ausgenutzt. Insbesondere kurz nach einer Diagnose wächst offenbar die Neigung, einfachen und eingängigen Botschaften zu glauben. »Sie greifen dann auch nach einem Strohhalm, statt auf wirksame Medikamente zu vertrauen.«
Zum anderen werden mit KI auch sogenannte Deep Fakes erstellt, etwa kleine Werbefilmchen, in denen vermeintlich echte, real existierende Ärzte konkrete Therapieratschläge geben. »Diese kann man mittlerweile nicht mehr als Fälschung erkennen«, sagt Johna. Hier fordert sie mehr politische Unterstützung für alle Betroffenen, nicht nur jene in der Medizin. Sie müssten bei der Löschung von solchen Beiträgen entlastet werden. Zudem müssten die Verursacher wirksam bestraft werden, was die Geschädigten kaum leisten könnten. »Wir brauchen mehr Pflichten für die Plattformen«, also mehr Regulierung.
Außerdem schade Desinformation der Wissenschaft. Nicht immer stecken aus Sicht von Johna finanzielle Interessen dahinter, wie etwa die von Unternehmen, die Nahrungsergänzungsmittel verkaufen. Es gibt auch andere, zum Beispiel »Überzeugungstäter aus den Reihen der Impfgegner«.
Die Varianten der Irreführung sind vielfältig. In der Corona-Pandemie etwa wurde längere Zeit das Entwurmungsmittel Ivermectin als Therapie gegen Sars-Cov2 angepriesen. Die Idee dazu geht auf Laborexperimente an Zellkulturen zurück. Dabei hemmten extrem hohe Dosen von Ivermectin die Vermehrung des Virus. Die verwendeten Mengen sind für Menschen jedoch giftig, und die Viren ließen sich so im Körper auch nicht sicher erreichen. Die Folge waren nicht wenige Vergiftungen von gutgläubigen Anwendern. Dabei ist Ivermectin in der zugelassenen Dosierung und bei ärztlicher Verschreibung ein sicheres Medikament, für Tiere – und auch für Menschen. In der Humanmedizin wird es gezielt gegen bestimmte Parasiten eingesetzt, wie bei Krätze (Skabies) oder der Flussblindheit in den Tropen, die durch Fadenwürmer bewirkt wird.
»Die Bevölkerung muss in die Lage versetzt werden, Dinge auch zu hinterfragen«, wünscht sich Johna, was schon mit Medienkompetenz im Schulunterricht anfängt.
Für die Ärzte selbst gibt es bereits spezielle Angebote, darunter Fortbildungen. Dabei geht es darum, Fehlinformationen überhaupt zu erkennen. Außerdem wird vermittelt, wie in der Praxis, also im Gespräch, Fakes strukturiert korrigiert werden können. Empfohlen wird auch, die eigene Qualifikation transparent darzustellen, etwa auf den Webseiten von Arztpraxen. Aber es geht ebenso um die Dokumentation verdächtiger Inhalte und Meldemöglichkeiten bei den digitalen Plattformen. »Das geht aber alles erst langsam los«, fasst Johna zusammen.
Ein Lichtblick ist immerhin, dass die Generalversammlung des Weltärztebundes im Oktober eine globale Richtlinie zur Bekämpfung medizinischer Fakes und Falschinformationen verabschiedete. Darin werden Tech-Konzerne, KI-Entwickler, Regierungen und auch die Mediziner selbst in die Pflicht genommen, der Welle von Desinformation entgegenzuwirken. So sollen etwa Plattformen Algorithmen zu stoppen, die medizinische Fake News gezielt hochspülen. Ärzte haben demnach die ethische Pflicht, Patienten und Öffentlichkeit mit wissenschaftlich fundierten, leicht verständlichen Informationen zu versorgen.
Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf
Bei uns muss niemand zahlen, um informiert zu sein. Klingt nach einem schlechten Geschäftsmodell? Ist es auch. Aber uns sind unabhängiger Journalismus und Teilhabe für alle wichtiger als Profit. Journalismus kostet trotzdem Geld: Recherche, Druck und all die Menschen, die ihn machen. Deshalb sind wir auf dich angewiesen. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro.
Spende einmalig oder regelmäßig, jeder Betrag zählt. Damit nd bleibt.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120374.title: UN-Verhandlungen | Weltklimagipfel in Zeiten des Stillstands
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120374.author: Jörg Staude
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120374.text:
- Wirtschaft und Umwelt
- UN-Verhandlungen
Weltklimagipfel in Zeiten des Stillstands
Im türkischen Antalya beginnt am Montag die COP 31. Es geht um Elektrifizierung, den Ausstieg aus Öl und Gas sowie Finanzhilfen für den globalen Süden.
Weltklimagipfel verbinden sich oft mit den Orten, in denen sie stattfinden: Bekanntestes Beispiel ist der in Paris 2015, in der Zählung die 21. Konferenz der Vertragsstaaten, (COP 21) – dort wurde der Klimavertrag verabschiedet. Auch der Gipfel 2021 im schottischen Glasgow verbindet sich mit einem klimapolitischen Meilenstein; zum ersten Mal bekannten sich alle Staaten dazu, auf den Ausstieg aus der fossilen Verbrennung hinzuarbeiten.
Der am Montag beginnende 31. Weltklimagipfel im türkischen Antalya, zu dem rund 40.000 Teilnehmer und Vertreter von rund 200 Staaten erwartet werden, verfügt schon jetzt über drei Neuerungen: Erstmals richten zwei Länder eine COP aus. Die Türkei stellt den Gipfelpräsidenten und betreut die sogenannte Action Agenda. Australien kümmert sich um die eigentlichen Verhandlungen. Außerdem ist das Pariser Klimaabkommen nach einem Jahrzehnt in ein umfassendes Regelwerk gegossen und muss nun in konkreten Klimapolitiken umgesetzt werden. Dabei ist die COP 31 die erste Konferenz, auf der Politik und Wissenschaft offiziell nicht mehr davon ausgehen, dass das Pariser 1,5-Grad-Ziel einzuhalten ist. Die Erde wird das Limit in den nächsten Jahren überschreiten und in einen zumindest zeitweiligen »Overshoot« eintreten.
Laut der Prognosen kann die Erhöhung der globalen Mitteltemperatur bis Ende des Jahrhunderts bestenfalls auf 1,8 Grad begrenzt werden. Sofern die Staaten nur die Klimamaßnahmen umsetzen, zu denen sie sich bisher verpflichtet haben, kommen wir bei 2,6 Grad heraus. Das Limit von 1,5 Grad gilt als eine Art Gefahren-Schwelle, nach deren Überschreiten viele Klima-Kipppunkte umzufallen drohen. Für den bestmöglichen Overshoot-Pfad müssen laut Klimaforschern die globalen Emissionen von Treibhausgasen (THG) bis 2030 um mindestens 18 Prozent gegenüber 2025 sinken und um knapp 70 Prozent bis 2040.
Tatsächlich wird derzeit nur mit einer THG-Minderung von 5 bis 8 Prozent bis 2030 gerechnet. Die Lücke wächst somit weiter – und wie die Milliarden Tonnen CO2 wieder aus der Atmosphäre geholt werden können, um den Overshoot abzubauen, ist völlig unklar.
Polykrise in der Klimakrise
Damit nicht genug. Die Weltgemeinschaft muss sich derzeit mit einer Vielzahl von Krisen herumschlagen: Geopolitische Spannungen steigen, bewaffnete Konflikte nehmen zu und das internationale Rechtssystem bröckelt. Dazu kommt die vom Iran-Krieg ausgelöste Energiepreiskrise. Auch wird es immer teurer, die Folgen von Extremwettern auszugleichen. Und das zu einer Zeit, in der sich der Spielraum der öffentlichen Haushalte zunehmend verengt. Darunter leidet auch die internationale Klimafinanzierung. Expert*innen sprechen von einer Polykrise in der Klimakrise. Die Welt stecke auch in einem politischen Overshoot.
Schnelle Besserung beim Klimaschutz ist nicht in Sicht. Zwar hält das rasante Wachstum der erneuerbaren Energien im Strom und zunehmend auch im Verkehr an. Die Hoffnung, dass so auch die Emissionen sinken würden, erfüllt sich bisher aber nicht. Der Grund ist der weiter steigende Energiebedarf in der Welt. Diesen kann der Zubau der Erneuerbaren abdecken, es gelingt aber nicht, fossile Energieträger spürbar zu ersetzen. Ferner ist der Zuwachs bei den Erneuerbaren global nicht gerecht verteilt. Die neuen Kapazitäten werden zu 86 Prozent in Asien, Europa und Nordamerika gebaut – gerade ärmere Weltregionen gehen leer aus.
Auf der COP 31 wird über zwei Initiativen beraten, die dieses Problem angehen sollen. Da ist zum einen TAFF. Die Abkürzung steht für Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels. Zahlreiche Staaten wollen als Fortsetzung des Glasgower Beschlusses einen konkreten, verbindlichen Fahrplan für den weltweiten Ausstieg aus Kohle, Öl und Gas vorantreiben. Angestoßen wurde dies bei der letztjährigen Klimakonferenz in Brasilien maßgeblich von Kolumbien und den Niederlanden.
Im April 2026 gab es dazu eine erste, weltweit beachtete Konferenz im kolumbianischen Santa Marta. Ziel von TAFF ist es, Staaten, Wissenschaft, Wirtschaft und Zivilgesellschaft zusammenzubringen, um den Übergang weg von fossilen Brennstoffen einzuleiten.
Ziel: 35 Prozent Stromanteil bis 2035
Die andere Initiative, die für Antalya Hoffnung verbreitet, ist das sogenannte Global Electrification Pledge. Nach dem Willen der Gastgeber sollen sich die Staaten verpflichten, bis 2035 mindestens 35 Prozent ihrer Endenergie durch Strom zu decken.
An dem Ziel hat selbst Deutschland ordentlich zu knabbern. Hierzulande liegt der Anteil des Stroms an der Endenergie erst bei rund 22 Prozent. Im Verkehr, beim Heizen und in der Industrie werden eben noch kräftig Öl und Gas verbrannt.
Ob Elektrifizierung dem Klima nutzt, hängt entscheidend davon ab, ob der Strom aus erneuerbaren Quellen stammt und effizient eingesetzt wird – der Zuwachs bei den Erneuerbaren darf also nicht vom steigenden Energiehunger kompensiert werden.
Vom Vorrang für Ökostrom will die türkische COP-Präsidentschaft aber offenbar nichts wissen. »Sie plant, sich nicht auf ein grünes, sondern nur auf ein allgemeines Ziel bei der Elektrifizierung festzulegen«, erklärt Ines Dombrowsky vom German Institute of Development and Sustainability. Die Ökonomin hält es für dringend, ein grünes Ziel einzufordern, kohärent zur TAFF-Initiative. »Ansonsten droht die Elektrifizierungsdebatte zu einer Ablenkung von anderen wichtigen Themen wie der Anpassungsfinanzierung zu führen«, befürchtet sie
Ob die Türkei und auch Australien bei den Verhandlungen doch eine grüne Elektrifizierung unterstützen, ist fraglich. Die Türkei ist der größte Kohleverstromer Europas, Australien ein führender Exporteur von Steinkohle und Flüssiggas.
Ein weiterer Makel haftet TAFF und auch dem Elektroziel an. Sie sind aktuell nur Teil der sogenannten Action Agenda. Das ist eine über Jahre gewachsene Sammlung zwischenstaatlicher Initiativen, auf die sich nicht alle Staaten, sondern nur unterschiedliche Koalitionen von Willigen einigen konnten.
Wirklich global verbindlich werden die 35x35-Elektro- und die TAFF-Initiative nur, wenn sie in offiziellen Beschlussdokumenten der COP auftauchen. Ob insbesondere die Staaten des globalen Südens dem zustimmen und der Gipfel in Antalya damit ein Erfolg wird, hängt für die Expert*innen entscheidend vom Entgegenkommen der Industrieländer bei der Klimafinanzierung ab. Hier sollen die jährlichen Mittel bekanntlich bis 2035 auf 300 Milliarden Dollar steigen. Nach aktuellen Angaben umfasste die Klimafinanzierung 2024 etwa 137 Milliarden Dollar.
Tatsächlich aber bestehe nur ein Drittel diese Gelder aus Zuschüssen, der Großteil seien Kredite, die oft auch zu Marktkonditionen gewährt werden, kritisiert Jan Kowalzig von der Entwicklungsorganisation Oxfam. Er räumt in dem Zusammenhang ein, dass Deutschland zwar noch immer zu den größten Geldgebern der Klimafinanzierung gehört, die Mittel wurden aber von jährlich 6 Milliarden auf aktuell 4,7 Milliarden Euro gekürzt. Für die nächsten Jahre sind weitere Streichungen programmiert. Zum Ausgleich will die Bundesregierung mehr Kredite gewähren und mehr private Mittel mobilisieren. Damit verschiebe sich aber der Schwerpunkt des Mitteleinsatzes, warnt Kowalzig. Geld würde dann verstärkt in die Energiewende in den Schwellenländern fließen und weniger in Wiederaufbau nach Naturkatastrophen oder in Klimaanpassung.
Absurder Streit um Mittel für Anpassung
Anpassung sei eben kein gewinnbringender »business case«, erläutert Sabine Minninger von der evangelischen Hilfsorganisation Brot für die Welt. »Einen Deich in Bangladesch zu bauen, bedeutet, dass der nächste Zyklon ihn wieder abräumen kann«, sagt die Klimaberaterin.
2024 dienten von den 137 Milliarden Euro Klimafinanzierung 35 Milliarden der Klimaanpassung. Um die Erhöhung dieser Mittel gibt es einen absurd anmutenden Streit zwischen Industrie- und Entwicklungsländern. Zwar ist bereits beschlossen, die Anpassungsmittel bis 2035 – als Teil des 300-Milliarden-Pakets – zu verdreifachen, nur werden sich die Länder nicht einig, von welcher Basis aus dies gerechnet werden soll. »Die Klimaanpassung hängt politisch in den Kniekehlen«, zeigt sich Minninger illusionslos. Der Streit um die Anpassung habe sogar das Potenzial, bereits zum Start die COP 31 zu lähmen.
Oxfam-Experte Kowalzig blickt ohnehin eher pessimistisch auf mögliche konkrete Ergebnisse: »Wir sehen jetzt schon, dass die Industrieländer überhaupt nicht bereit sind, bei der Klimafinanzierung irgendetwas zu machen.« Das würden wiederum einige der Petrostaaten als taktischen Hebel nutzen, um Fortschritte an anderer Stelle zu verhindern. Das sei schon die letzten Jahre so gewesen. »Solange die Industrieländer nicht bereit sind, sich bei der Finanzierung zu öffnen, wird es auch anderswo keine Fortschritte geben«, prognostiziert Kowalzig.
In dem Punkt würde sich der Gipfel in Antalya dann nicht von vielen seiner Vorläufer unterscheiden. Er könnte trotz des Overshoots zum Symbol des Stillstands werden.
Wir haben nachgerechnet
Dieser Artikel hat dich nichts gekostet. Uns schon: Recherche, Produktion und Technik. Wir haben bei der Büromiete sowie bei Druck und Vertrieb gespart. Und wir haben auf Gehalt verzichtet. Trotzdem gilt: Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro. Du zahlst, was du kannst, dafür schreiben wir weiter.
Keine Paywall, kein Kleingedrucktes, nur ein Ziel: dass nd bleibt.

https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.title: Another No 1 falls as Notre Dame hold off Miami to shake up college football playoff race
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.author: Agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/n.text:
CJ Carr threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns as No 4 Notre Dame avenged their most damaging loss of last season, racing to a 21-point lead before holding on to beat top-ranked Miami 31-24 on Saturday night.
Micah Gilbert caught two of Carr’s touchdown passes, Jordan Faison had the other and Nolan James Jr added a rushing score for Notre Dame (8-1, No 11 College Football Playoff), who entered the game knowing another defeat to Miami could derail their national championship hopes.
The Hurricanes (8-1, No 1 CFP) started slowly on offense in their first game without injured wide receiver and Heisman Trophy hopeful Malachi Toney. Notre Dame, whose 27-24 loss to Miami last season ultimately kept them out of the playoff, never trailed.
“I’m happy for this university,” Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman said in a televised on-field interview. “I’m happy for our players. There’s a lot of support from Notre Dame Nation and this is special moment for them. ... They’re a dang good football team and they beat a dang good football team.”
Darian Mensah threw three touchdown passes for Miami, twice bringing the Hurricanes within seven points after they had trailed 24-3 early in the third quarter. Cooper Barkate caught two of those passes, while Elija Lofton had the other.
Lofton nearly hauled in another touchdown that would have made it 31-30 – the same score as the teams’ famous 1988 meeting – with 3:36 remaining. He appeared to make a fourth-down catch in the end zone and get both feet down, but Notre Dame’s Luke Talich, who had intercepted Mensah in the third quarter, knocked the ball away.
Officials ruled that Lofton had not completed the catch. Notre Dame took over on downs, ran the clock down to about a minute and held on for the victory.
Miami coach Mario Cristobal said he was “beyond upset” that Lofton’s apparent catch had not been ruled a touchdown.
“Obviously, a tough loss to take,” Cristobal said. “Proud of our players for the resilience. ... Don’t leave it in the hands of the officials. Play better. Coach better. Find a way to win.”
Miami’s defeat left just two unbeaten teams in the Football Bowl Subdivision: Utah and UCLA, who both improved to 9-0 with victories on Saturday. It marked the first time since 2003 that only two teams had made it through their first nine games unbeaten, when TCU and Oklahoma achieved the feat.
A capacity crowd packed Notre Dame Stadium on a bitterly cold night, with temperatures falling from 40F at kickoff into the mid-30s. Forty-three NFL scouts were also in attendance as the Irish delivered their biggest victory of the season.
Miami had a chance to cut into Notre Dame’s lead in the second quarter after reaching first-and-goal at the Irish one-yard line. But three rushing attempts – one by Mark Fletcher Jr and two quarterback keepers by Mensah – went nowhere, forcing the Hurricanes to settle for a field goal.
Miami trailed 17-3 at halftime, having scored at least 14 first-half points and averaged 27 before the break in their first eight games.
Notre Dame also pulled out all the stops for the occasion, honoring a host of former stars including Joe Montana, Jerome Bettis Sr, Tony Rice, Chris Zorich, Ricky Watters and Ron Powlus. NBA president of basketball operations Byron Spruell was among those recognized, along with Pat Murphy, manager of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers and a former Notre Dame baseball coach.
The victory carried historical echoes of Notre Dame’s famous 31-30 upset of top-ranked Miami in the 1988 “Catholics vs Convicts” game. The Hurricanes fell to 44-7 all-time when ranked No 1 in the AP Top 25, including an 0-2 record against the Irish.
Notre Dame improved to 10-17-1 against No 1 teams, claiming their first such victory in exactly six years. Their previous win came against top-ranked Clemson on 7 November 2020, when the Tigers were without star quarterback Trevor Lawrence.
The Irish host Boston College next Saturday, while Miami return home to face Duke.

https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.title: Messi claims second straight Golden Boot as Nashville sets points record on MLS Decision Day
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.author: Agencies
https://www.theguardian.com/football/202.text:
Lionel Messi won his second consecutive MLS Golden Boot award on Saturday, but Inter Miami squandered a three-goal lead in a 3-3 draw with Charlotte on the final day of the regular season.
The Argentine superstar failed to score but set up Miami’s first two goals from corners at Nu Stadium as the defending champions secured second place in the Eastern Conference and home-field advantage for the first two rounds of the playoffs.
Messi’s 26 goals made him the first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boot awards. Dallas forward Petar Musa finished second with 22 after failing to score in his team’s 3-1 home victory over Colorado.
Ian Fray, Luis Suárez and Rodrigo De Paul scored first-half goals for Miami before Liel Abada struck twice shortly after the break to spark a Charlotte comeback, completed by Rodolfo Aloko’s 90th-minute equalizer.
Nashville broke the MLS single-season points record with a 2-0 victory over Cincinnati, finishing with 77 points to surpass the previous mark of 74 set by Miami in 2024.
Nashville finished atop the Eastern Conference with 23 wins, three defeats and eight draws, while Miami took second place with 60 points. Third-place New England missed a chance to overtake Miami after suffering a surprise 1-0 defeat at Orlando, leaving them on 58 points.
Miami will face Columbus in the opening round of the playoffs. Elsewhere in the East, New England will meet Philadelphia, Charlotte will take on Chicago and top-seeded Nashville will face the winner of the wild-card matchup between Orlando and Cincinnati.
Columbus secured seventh place and avoided the wild-card round with a 4-3 victory at Chicago.
At Nu Stadium, Messi’s 14th-minute corner fell unexpectedly to Charlotte’s Luca de la Torre, whose attempted clearance popped up for Fray to open the scoring.
Another Messi corner in the 33rd minute found Suárez unmarked at the near post, where the Uruguayan glanced a header into the net to double Miami’s advantage.
De Paul made it 3-0 before half-time, but Abada pulled one back for Charlotte shortly after the restart and struck again in the 55th minute.
Aloko completed the comeback in the 90th minute, reacting quickest after Smalls’s shot rebounded off the post.
A visibly frustrated Messi struck the woodwork in stoppage time before Aloko came within inches of an improbable winner with a thunderous shot into the side-netting.
Seattle and Real Salt Lake advance in West
Western Conference champions Vancouver defeated Canadian rivals Montreal 2-0 to finish second in the overall standings, securing home-field advantage should the Whitecaps face Inter Miami in a rematch of last year’s MLS Cup final.
Six teams entered Decision Day fighting for the final three Western Conference playoff places, with all 30 MLS clubs in action.
Portland, Colorado and the LA Galaxy each needed only a victory to secure a playoff berth, but only the Timbers delivered, winning 2-0 at Austin.
Real Salt Lake defeated the Galaxy 2-1, while Colorado fell 3-1 at Dallas, allowing Salt Lake to claim a postseason place.
Seattle secured the other remaining berth with a 2-1 home victory over Los Angeles FC. Albert Rusnák scored in the opening minute and set up Sebastián Gómez’s 31st-minute goal before Eddie Segura pulled one back for LAFC in the 82nd minute.
Minnesota defeated visiting San Jose 3-1 but, like the Galaxy, finished a point behind Real Salt Lake and missed the playoffs.
The opening Western Conference playoff matchups pit Vancouver against the winner of the wild-card meeting between Seattle and Real Salt Lake, Dallas against Portland, LAFC against St Louis and Houston against San Jose.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: Trump says he asked Dana White, UFC boss, to be his new White House press secretary
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Robert Mackey
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Donald Trump has offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, the president said in a social media post on Saturday.
Trump described White, who staged a cage-fighting spectacle at the White House to mark the president’s 80th birthday in June, as “a violent Fighter and Warrior”, credentials unlike any ever used to describe previous press secretaries.
Trump added that he asked White, a vocal supporter who campaigned for him in 2024, to bring six UFC fighters with him to serve as press aides. “We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” Trump wrote. “Dana, please take the job!”
It was initially unclear whether the job offer was part of an actual plan, or an attention-grabbing stunt from a president desperate to change the subject from the huge losses suffered by his party in elections this week.
There was no immediate response from White, who, some observers noted, might hesitate to leave a lucrative role running the UFC, which has earned him a fortune estimated to be in excess of $600m, for a job in government service that pays $195,000 a year.
Later on Saturday, after CNN reported that White had declined the offer and that one aide to the president had described it as a joke, White posted an Instagram story with an image of himself in the White House briefing room above the caption: “On to the next chapter.”
The UFC boss was then asked about the president’s post at a news conference after a boxing match in London on Saturday night. “I’m flying to Washington DC right now” to meet with Trump, White replied, without saying whether he would accept the job. “I’m going to meet with him, we have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that,” he added.
The president’s Truth Social post was illustrated by seven images, including what appeared to be an AI-generated image of White behind the presidential seal in a press room, and photographs of the six UFC fighters whom Trump fantasizes about deploying to deal with reporters who ask him awkward questions: Islam Makhachev and Khabib Nurmagomedov (who are both from a Muslim-majority region of Russia), Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes and Kayla Harrison – whose last name was mistakenly rendered as “Harris” by the president.
In his post, Trump acknowledged that two of his dream hires, Makhachev and Nurmagomedov, are not Americans, but he did not mention that Nurmagomedov is reportedly close to the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, or that Makhachev has spoken out in defense of Palestinian civilians killed by Israel in Gaza. In 2023, Makhachev also celebrated a victory in one fight by saying, “Alhamdulillah,” the Arabic phrase for “praise be to God” used by Muslims. Democrat Abdul El-Sayed was criticized in the rightwing media for using that same Arabic phrase in his victory speech this week.
The first in a series of taxpayer-funded pro-Trump ads broadcast by the White House in the run-up to the recent midterms closed with images of the UFC fight on Trump’s birthday and remarks about him from White, who could be heard saying: “He is the toughest, most resilient human being I have ever met in my life.” White used that formulation to describe Trump multiple times during the 2024 presidential election campaign, most notably to sing Trump’s praises at the Republican national convention.
The role of White House press secretary has been vacant for three weeks, since Trump’s previous pick, far-right commentator Katie Zacharia, was forced to resign after trying, and failing, to dodge questions about why she described herself as an attorney despite having failed the bar exam.
Henry Smith contributed reporting

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
Tearful Alex Eala loses Hong Kong Open final to Claire Liu in straight sets
Philippine’ tennis star Eala was left stunned after a 6-3, 6-0 loss to the 102-ranked American in Hong Kong.
Tennis trailblazer Alex Eala from the Philippines burst into tears as she reflected on a “life-changing” season after falling agonisingly short of a second WTA Tour title in Hong Kong.
The second seed was stunned 6-3, 6-0 by Claire Liu in the final of the Hong Kong Open as the American, ranked 102nd, won her first tour title on Sunday.
Eala is at a career-high 17 in the world after a breakout year in which the 21-year-old clinched her maiden title, in Washington, DC, in August.
That victory made her the first player from the Philippines to win a tournament on the WTA Tour.
Eala, set to rise to world number 15 next week, started the year ranked 50th.
“This season has changed my life; it’s changed my life for the better,” Eala, who finished the final with heavy strapping on her right leg, told the crowd afterwards.
Becoming emotional as she addressed her team in the stands, she said: “I’m incredibly proud of the work we’ve put in this year.
“We’re the only ones that truly know what it took to arrive to this point in our journey.
“This is only the beginning.”

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.title: US task force to cut off Iran’s transport of advanced weapons: What we know
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.text:
US task force to cut off Iran’s transport of advanced weapons: What we know
As fears of an escalation grow, Washington announces ‘Task Force Iron Gate’.
As the threat of renewed war grows, Washington is expanding efforts to choke Tehran’s military supply networks, including through Task Force Iron Gate – a unit targeting land routes and the Caspian Sea.
With it, the US military is trying to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials, the United States Central Command (CENTCOM) announced on Saturday.
The same day, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced ambitious plans for underground complexes capable of sustaining missile and drone production under bombardment. That announcement came amid reports of ongoing construction near Iranian missile bases, based on satellite imagery and previous claims by Tehran that US strikes failed to destroy its underground facilities.
Here’s what we know about the US task force:
What is the purpose of the task force?
Task Force Iron Gate will aim to find out where “weapons systems are coming in, how they could potentially be cut off” and how “Iran is transporting its energy”, Michael Mulroy, a former US deputy assistant defence secretary for the Middle East, told Al Jazeera.
It expands on the US blockade of Iranian ports to cover Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea and will reportedly be run by 20 civilian and military personnel.
Iran shares borders with seven countries – Afghanistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Pakistan Turkiye and Turkmenistan.
Based in Tampa, Florida, the unit will coordinate with other US government agencies “on preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and illegal revenue streams across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea”, CENTCOM said. Task Force Iron Gate will reinforce “the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea”, CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper said.
If US President Donald Trump ramps up the war, there will likely be attacks on this “series of targets”, said Mulroy.
“Unlike Operation Epic Fury, which primarily (focused) on military targets, I think these targets will be focused on economic and infrastructure targets, as part of this comprehensive plan to cut the regime off from its ability to fight and ability to fund itself,” Mulroy said. “It’s primarily a coordination body that’s looking for how the US can increase its economic strangulation strategy by going after the ground routes as they’ve already covered a majority of the maritime routes.”
How has Iran responded to CENTCOM’s announcement?
The IRGC dismissed the US military plan as “just a play on words”.
“The Americans cannot achieve their goal through this, which is to apply severe economic pressure to collapse and disintegrate the Iranian economy,” said IRGC spokesman Sardar Mohebi, as reported by the Fars news agency.
Washington previously “claimed that Iran will suffer an economic collapse within two weeks, but we witnessed that this did not happen”, he added.
Is the task force a response to reports of Russia-Iran weapons ties?
While CENTCOM’s announcement did not explicitly identify Iran’s weapons trade with Russia, analysts say the unit could be seen as an attempt to disrupt supply networks that include Russian connections.
US media have reported that Russia has sent drone components and explosives to Iran via the Caspian Sea. There are also claims that Russian technology could be helping Iran develop advanced supersonic cruise missiles.
Mahjoob Zweiri, a professor of contemporary history and politics at Qatar University, told Al Jazeera that reports of military equipment imported via Russia are a “real concern” for the United States.
The task force therefore could “cause a confrontation with Russia”, he said.
Rami Khouri, a public policy fellow at the American University of Beirut and a non-resident senior fellow at the Arab Center in Washington, said of the new unit: “The US really doesn’t quite know what to do about Iran as we’ve seen, and it’s doing things off the cuff” – a strategy that has led to little success.
Can the US really choke off Iran’s supply lines?
Khouri pointed to Iran’s history as a trading nation for thousands of years as evidence that the US mission is near impossible.
“There’s an enormous web of contacts that Iran has had for thousands of years with traders and partners and allies all over the region, especially in Asia – it’s virtually impossible for the US to seal off every one,” he said.
While the US can impose a blockade or sanctions on Iran, it cannot control the behaviour of everyone from the Russians, to the Chinese, to the Emiratis and beyond, said the analyst.
“There are people all over the region who have links with Iran, some very close, some just commercial,” he said.
A lot of the materials that go into Iran’s weapons systems are bought from some other countries, – some even from the US or Europeans – and then they are channelled through companies in Asia, Khouri added.
Could this change the course of the war?
Former Trump aide and top counterterrorism official Joe Kent, who resigned in March due to the US’s war on Iran, said the new task force is an attempt by CENTCOM to subvert ongoing diplomatic efforts.
“This is CENTCOM inviting Iran to escalate while the vice president is attempting to negotiate with the Iranians,” Kent posted on X. “This is, as CENTCOM calls it, ‘policy by CONOP’, when the military finds a way to subvert the White House without blatantly disobeying the President, by taking actions that will ensure a war escalates or perpetuates.”
According to The Wall Street Journal, CENTCOM chief Cooper is among the many officials, alongside Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, pressing Trump to renew attacks on Iran.
The task force may also just be symbolic because the US has no military presence on the Caspian Sea, said Zweiri.
“America has no access to the sea, unless some of the neighbouring countries like Azerbaijan or Armenia or others collaborate [with them] … And they’re not collaborating on this because they don’t want to upset Russia,” he said. “It will require … troops on the ground, and this is unlikely to happen.”
Zweiri also said that the Caspian Sea’s contribution to Iran’s economy is just 11 percent, so the task force’s actions won’t have much negative impact on Tehran.
Al Jazeera could not independently verify this figure but the Caspian Sea accounts for only a fraction of Iran’s overall maritime trade, according to the Soufan Center based in New York City.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.text:
At least 21 dead as small boat sinks off Senegal
Senegalese Interior Ministry says one person rescued as search operation continues after migrant vessel capsized.
A small boat carrying migrants and refugees has sunk off northwestern Senegal, killing at least 21 people.
The Senegalese Interior Ministry said in a statement on Sunday that one person had been rescued in addition to the 21 bodies recovered.
The ministry said the death toll was “provisional” as of late Saturday, adding that the search was still ongoing and the families of the victims were being helped.
Media reports said the pirogue-type flat-bottomed boat capsized on Saturday off the Loumpoul dunes in the Kebemer department, between Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis.
Le Soleil newspaper said that most of the victims were from the Leona and Thieppe districts in the same department.
Thousands of people have died in recent years attempting to reach Spain’s Canary Islands from West Africa, including 635 in the first five months of this year, according to migrant rights group Walking Borders
Spanish authorities on the Canary Island of El Hierro declared an emergency on Saturday after a surge in migrant boat arrivals. Since the start of November, El Hierro authorities said more than 3,300 people had arrived aboard around 30 boats.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.title: Egypt’s reopening of its embassy in Tripoli signals regional shift on Libya
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/8.text:
Egypt’s reopening of its embassy in Tripoli signals regional shift on Libya
Former rivals in Libya are pushing for a unity government to end years of conflict.
The reopening of the Egyptian embassy in Tripoli marks a fundamental political shift, both domestically and regionally, for Libya, analysts say.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty inaugurated the historic embassy building on Saturday, which had been closed for 12 years due to security concerns.
Libya has been politically divided since the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, with rival administrations formed in Tripoli in the west and Tobruk and Benghazi in the east.
Egypt was widely considered to be backing the eastern authority, effectively led by strongman and renegade military commander Khalifa Haftar, and his self-styled Libyan National Army (LNA), until recent regional developments led Cairo to rethink its approach.
Libyan political analyst Hazem al-Rayes said the reopening of the embassy in Tripoli – which was the seat of the internationally recognised government that Haftar was fighting – is a sign of this.
“I can consider that what Egypt is doing in its recent moves towards the capital, Tripoli, is an attempt to readjust its behaviour in the Libyan file … [for] five years, no Egyptian foreign minister visited the capital,” he told Al Jazeera.
Elias al-Barouni, a political science professor at Libya’s Nalut University, also believes the move goes beyond the resumption of regular consular services in Tripoli.
“We are facing an indicator of a shift in Cairo’s method of managing its relations with the Libyan parties, and a rearrangement of its priorities in dealing with the Libyan crisis,” al-Barouni told Al Jazeera.
There have been several significant political and regional shifts that have somewhat stabilised the volatile situation in Libya, where thousands have been killed in fighting between militias attached to rival political authorities.
In July 2026, Ankara and the LNA reached unprecedented coordination, spearheading agreements to develop military facilities, advanced surveillance systems, and training programmes in Turkiye for eastern Libyan officers.
The deputy commander of eastern Libyan forces and Haftar’s son, Saddam Haftar, has also paid visits to regional capitals, including Turkiye and Qatar, which have supported the United Nations-recognised Government of National Accord (GNA) in Tripoli.
In Libya, rivals recently signed the so-called “4+4 agreement” that sets out a roadmap for possible presidential and legislative elections over the next two years.
Badr Hassan al-Shafei, a professor of African studies and conflict resolution at Cairo University, told Al Jazeera that Egypt came to revisit its policy towards Libya after realising that its reliance on eastern forces, led by Haftar, was not conducive to its overall strategic interests.
“It is clear that Cairo … found that relying on one party or leaning towards one party in Libya, which is Haftar’s party, may not be the right bet perhaps at the present time or even for a while, since the Turkish intervention several years ago,” al-Shafei told Al Jazeera.
“Consequently, perhaps Egypt wants to create a balance or also send a message to Haftar that he should not act unilaterally and that acting should be in coordination with Cairo, so it worked to extend bridges of cooperation with Libya also …”
Egypt has also become more concerned about developments to the south of its border, particularly the expansion of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan, which had allegedly received support from Haftar.
“Today, Egypt is no longer the Egypt of five years ago when its policies and relations were limited only to the [eastern] authorities in Benghazi,” al-Rayes told Al Jazeera.
It is “convinced today that its ally [LNA], which it supported throughout the past years at the expense of the legitimate government in Tripoli … has distanced itself from it today, and it needs to readjust its political behaviour with Tripoli and with the legitimate government”, he said.
Maritime border disputes
During Abdelatty’s visit to Tripoli, he discussed critical economic files with Libyan officials, including the 2019 maritime border memorandum of understanding signed between Tripoli and Ankara.
According to the Facebook page of the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Abdelatty reaffirmed the importance of addressing Egyptian concerns regarding maritime demarcation between Libya and Turkiye in light of international law. The eastern parliament recently ratified the maritime agreement, which it initially opposed.
“Consequently, perhaps Cairo is trying to prevent the ratification of this agreement from causing damage to its interests in gas and oil exploration in the Eastern Mediterranean, and from that it wanted to extend bridges to Tripoli as well,” al-Shafei said.
“Instead of limiting itself to political and diplomatic objection from outside Tripoli, Cairo has become negotiating directly with the Libyan government that signed the agreement.”
Egypt might also be attracted to opportunities that reconstruction and the revival of Libya’s oil industry might bring.
“Perhaps with the reconstruction process, the incoming Egyptian labour will have priority, or even the currently present one will have its living conditions improved, not to mention the idea of the possibility of Egyptian investments and companies entering the reconstruction process,” al-Shafei said.
Push for settlement
After years of backing rival sides, a new regional consensus means there is a greater likelihood of rivals in Libya reaching a comprehensive agreement to end the war, al-Rayes told Al Jazeera.
But al-Barouni cautioned that there is still a plethora of issues facing Libya, and only a comprehensive solution can end the divisions within Libya.
“The Libyan problem is not merely a dispute over the name of the head of government, but rather it is a dispute over the nature of power, the distribution of influence, control over institutions and resources, the future of the military institution, and the conditions for reaching elections,” al-Barouni said.
“If Cairo, Ankara, Washington, and other capitals agree on the necessity of ending the division, that is a development that can be built upon, but the success of any settlement remains linked to the ability of the Libyans to formulate an independent national project. Libya needs a settlement that ends the division, not a deal that redistributes the division.”

https://www.theguardian.com/environment/.title: Cop31 must deliver climate progress that people can see is real, host says
https://www.theguardian.com/environment/.author: Adam Morton in Melbourne, and Fiona Harvey, Oliver Milman and Graham Readfearn in Antalya
https://www.theguardian.com/environment/.text:
The Cop31 summit must produce progress, “a tangible outcome ... that people can see is real”, its host has said as scores of world leaders and representatives of close to 190 countries gather in Turkey for the UN climate talks.
The high-stakes meeting begins on Monday, as countries around the world grapple with the strongest El Niño weather system on record, supercharged by fossil fuels, which is set to take hundreds of thousands of lives and cause damage costing trillions of dollars.
Friction is expected between the rich and poor worlds over who pays for the impacts of the climate crisis, and the slow pace of cutting greenhouse gas emissions. Temperatures have broken records this year, surpassing the limit of 1.5C above preindustrial levels aimed for in the 2015 Paris climate agreement.
Adão Soares Barbosa, the chair of the Least Developed Countries, a negotiating group of 44 nations, said: “Keeping 1.5C within reach by minimising the duration and magnitude of the overshoot, delivering accessible and predictable climate finance, strengthening adaptation, and addressing loss and damage [caused to poor countries by extreme weather] are not political choices but matters of survival. The credibility of the Paris agreement will be measured not by promises made, but by commitments fulfilled, and lives protected in vulnerable countries.”
Unusually, the talks will have dual hosts: they will take place in the Turkish city of Antalya but the formal negotiations will be presided over by Australia, following a compromise reached last year over their competing bids.
Chris Bowen, Australia’s climate and energy minister and president of negotiations for Cop31, told the Guardian in an interview: “We need a tangible outcome focused on implementation [of emissions cuts and finance] that people can see is real. We need progress, it needs to be a step forward on previous Cops.”
Australia also wants a “strong, ambitious outcome” to raise the plight of low-lying countries in the Pacific region for whom the climate crisis poses an existential threat. “We need to finally elevate some of the issues so important to our Pacific family,” Bowen said. “[Only] 0.2% of the world’s available climate finance goes to small island developing states for adaptation, for countries whose very existence is at stake.”
But climate advocates and more than 500 scientists in Australia said Australia must stop approving coalmines and gas projects if it wanted to escape the charge of hypocrisy.
The summit will have a notable absentee, with the US refusing to send a delegation for the second year in a row. The Trump administration wants no part of “extremist climate policies” embraced by other countries, according to a White House spokesperson.
Donald Trump expressed glee shortly before the US midterm elections about the huge profits made by oil and gas companies due to the Iran war, which he started and has caused an increase in living costs around the world. “I don’t give a damn,” the president said at a recent rally in Georgia. “I’m going to say it: we’re making a frickin’ fortune.”
However, a group of 20 Democratic members of Congress have made the trip to Antalya, buoyed by their party’s stunning success in the US midterms last week that will enable them to stymie Trump’s attempts to dismantle pollution rules and withhold financial support for clean energy.
Developing countries and civil society will seek to put climate finance and justice at the heart of the Cop31 talks. Rukiya Khamis, the east Africa programme manager at the 350.org campaigning group, said: “Across east Africa, people are facing the devastating impacts of a climate crisis they did not cause. From prolonged droughts to destructive floods, we are losing homes, livelihoods and access to food and water. Yet the money needed to respond to these impacts remains out of reach for many of the countries and communities most affected. It is fundamentally unjust that those least responsible are being left to carry the greatest costs.”
This summer more than 50,000 people died in Europe due to heatwaves, severe wildfire smoke shrouded swathes of North America and a glacier collapse in Nepal triggered a landslide that caused more than 1,500 deaths, while the El Niño weather event, described as “staggering” by scientists and still to reach its peak, is gathering strength.
However, while the pace of progress on cutting global emissions has been slow, the Iran war has spurred many countries to see fossil fuels as expensive and vulnerable to shocks, while renewables continue to plummet in price.
Simon Stiell, the UN’s climate chief, said before the talks: “Climate impacts hit every population and every economy harder each year. [But] almost every major economy, and many medium-sized and smaller economies, now see climate action as a central driver of economic growth, jobs, and affordable and secure energy.”
Cop host Turkey also wants more countries to switch to electric technologies, such as electric vehicles and heat pumps, as these are many times more efficient than their fossil fuel counterparts. A target for 35% of global final energy to come from electricity by 2035 will be on the table, but faces opposition from some.
Both presidency countries rely heavily on fossil fuels. Australia is one of the world’s leading exporters of coal and liquefied natural gas. The centre-left Labor government has targets to reach net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, and have more than 80% of its electricity generated by solar and wind by 2030, but is off track to meet them.
Labor also faces a political threat from the resurgent rightwing One Nation party, which dismisses climate science. One Nation and the Liberal and National party coalition want to scrap the net zero goal.
The UK energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, said: “This summer, we all felt it: climate change is here, in Britain, now. No country can tackle it alone, which is why Cop31 matters. The answer to high bills and climate change is the same – more clean, homegrown power, creating good jobs and warmer homes. Cop31 is about Britain’s national interest.”
